records.name: Charles Francis Adams
records.bio: Adams appears in the Auckland procurement chain as the person who physically delivered Ward-linked Blaschka models in 1885. A triangular settlement also connected Auckland, Adams and Ward, so the project treats him as a preparator and delivery actor rather than as maker or seller.

records.name: Alfred William Alcock
records.bio: Alfred William Alcock was superintendent of the Indian Museum in Calcutta. An official 1894 guide signed by him documents the Invertebrate Gallery and its glass-model displays, linking a named museum administrator to the later display history of a verified Blaschka customer.

records.name: Frank Collins Baker
records.bio: Baker was an American malacologist whose early twentieth-century work intersects the documented history of the Museo Nacional de México Blaschka collection. His record helps connect later zoological study and museum documentation to a collection acquired decades earlier.

records.name: P. T. Barnum
records.bio: Tufts archival research states that Barnum purchased Blaschka sea creatures in 1885 for exhibition in the Barnum Museum of Natural History. The purchase year, purchaser and purpose are strong; the exact model count, price and dealer route remain open.
records.open: The exact model count, price and dealer route for the 1885 Tufts purchase remain unresolved.

records.name: Louis C. Bierweiler
records.bio: Bierweiler was a Harvard-associated curator whose 1931 European journey included a documented visit to Rudolf Blaschka at Hosterwitz. His surviving travel diary, notes, receipts, ephemera and photographs offer an unusually continuous later view of the workshop and its institutional visitors.

records.name: Joseph William Blankinship
records.bio: Blankinship was a botanist and Rudolf Blaschka’s field companion during the 1895 United States journey. His place in the project is tied to the second American field campaign and the movement of botanical observations and material back toward the workshop.

records.name: Karolina Blaschka
records.bio: Karolina is visible in the surviving archive as part of the workshop household and, more cautiously, its knowledge infrastructure. Family papers and correspondence place her inside Rudolf’s working and visitor world, but the present evidence does not justify attributing model making or scientific authorship to her.
records.open: Extent of her recurrent role in workshop visitors, correspondence and knowledge mediation beyond the documented household evidence.

records.name: Leopold Blaschka
records.bio: Leopold moved from the family glass trade into scientific model making in the 1860s. Early botanical work, sea-anemone models and later zoological catalogues turned the Dresden workshop into an international supplier of study objects; this project follows the observation, making, cataloguing and commercial records around that work.

records.name: Rudolf Blaschka
records.bio: Rudolf joined the workshop in the 1870s and increasingly carried its scientific and technical work. His 1892 and 1895 American field trips connected botanical observation, collecting and drawing to work in Hosterwitz, and after Leopold’s death he continued the Harvard botanical commission.
